title: Avalanche
tldr: Stay out of avalanche terrain when conditions are unsafe. Read the local avalanche forecast before travel and choose a safer route; rescue equipment does not make a dangerous slope safe. If someone is buried, call rescue and start companion rescue only where you can avoid another avalanche.
steps: Consult the local avalanche center and get training before entering snow-covered backcountry.
Avoid avalanche paths and slopes identified in the forecast; turn around when uncertain.
Each person needs a transceiver, probe and shovel and practiced companion rescue skills.
Note the last seen location, call rescue and assess continuing danger before searching.
next: Take a practical avalanche course and travel with trained partners. Use professional local advice for route selection.
watch: Do not enter unstable terrain for an untrained rescue that may create more victims.
review_status: source-linked editorial review; not independent expert certification
without_help: Without a working phone, prevention and trained companion rescue are even more important. Stay on terrain you have assessed as safe; do not enter a dangerous slope to find reception. Carry a written route and turnaround time with a trusted contact.
household: Account for children, older people, pets and anyone who needs assistance before moving. Keep shoes, medicines and a torch in the shelter area. Decide who helps whom and who carries the essential supplies; do not send a lone child to retrieve items.
pack_now: Keep essential medicines, drinking water, a battery light, shoes, phone power and a written contact card within reach. Adapt the load to the hazard and the people with you; do not delay escape to collect equipment.
